class.name: SnowCover3D
class.brief_description: A snowpack that follows the camera: snow falls, settles, ages, melts, slides and drifts by the weather.
class.description: A square map of snowpack cells, [member extent] metres wide, that follows the camera (or [member follow_target]). Each cell holds its snow water equivalent, density, liquid water and albedo, and advances them from the active [code]WeatherMap3D[/code] (its precipitation, temperature, humidity, wind, cloud and sun) or, without one, from this node's own weather settings. - Rain or snow: the logistic model of air temperature and humidity of Jennings et al. (2018), the air cooling with height by [member lapse_rate], so mountains get a snow line. - New snow density by temperature (Hedstrom and Pomeroy 1998); settling toward a maximum density that grows with depth, and albedo ageing (CLASS, Verseghy 1991). - Melt by temperature and by the sunlight each slope absorbs (Pellicciotti et al. 2005); rain and meltwater held up to [member liquid_capacity], the rest running off; refreezing in the cold, into crusts that harden with each melt-freeze cycle ([member crust_enabled]). - Snow sliding off slopes steeper than [member slide_angle] (SnowSlide, Bernhardt and Schulz 2010) and wind drifting it into sheltered ground (Winstral, Elder and Davis 2002), and moving the snow already lying ([member wind_transport_enabled]). Materials read it through the [code]snow_map[/code] and [code]snow_map_rect[/code] global shader parameters ([member BaseMaterial3D.snow_enabled]), in raster and under path tracing; scripts through the [code]get_*_at[/code] methods. Cells entering the map as it moves take the state of the nearest cell that was inside it. The last [SnowCover3D] to enter the tree publishes the map.

method.name: add_crust
method.description: Lays a frozen crust [param thickness] m thick (at most 0.05) on top of the snow everywhere on the map, as if it had been through [param cycles] melt-freeze cycles. For scenes that start on crusted snow. See [method crust_strength].

method.name: add_snow
method.description: Adds [param swe_mm] of snow water equivalent everywhere on the map at [param density] (kg/m³), as fresh snow. For scenes that start under snow.

method.name: advance
method.description: Advances the snowpack by [param seconds] of weather time at once, in steps of up to 10 minutes, then publishes the snow map. Wind-drift data is baked first if it is missing, so the result does not depend on frame timing.

method.name: advance_world
method.description: Runs the world tier forward [param seconds] of weather time now (it otherwise advances every [member world_update_every] updates).

method.name: bake_climate
method.description: Runs [member climate]'s season over the square [param rect] at [param resolution] cells a side, on this cover's ground and settings, and stores the snowpack it leaves in the climate. The world tier then starts from it and the near square is seeded from it. Blocking: a 182-day winter on 256 x 256 cells takes a few seconds.

method.name: canopy_capacity
method.description: The most snow water a canopy of [param closure] holds, in mm (kg/m²), for new snow of [param snow_density] kg/m³ (Hedstrom and Pomeroy 1998).

method.name: clear
method.description: Removes all snow from the map.

method.name: cornice_crack_rate
method.description: How fast the tension crack behind a cornice opens, in m/day: the slab tilts about its root by viscous creep, at the snow viscosity of Crocus (Vionnet et al. 2012) for its temperature [param celsius] and water. A 4 m cornice opens about 0.9 cm a day at -5 °C, 1.4 at 0 °C and 4.9 wet, as at Gruvefjellet (0.4 to 2.8 cm a day, up to 8.6 before a failure; Vogel et al. 2012), faster as the crack opens.

method.name: cornice_growth_share
method.description: How fast a cornice grows at a wind of [param wind_ratio] times the threshold for moving snow, as a share of the fastest: 0 below 1 and from 2, 1 at 1.4 (Yu et al. 2023).

method.name: cornice_root_stress
method.description: The tensile stress at the root of a cornice [param length] m long whose tension crack is [param crack] m open, in kPa, with [param liquid] the pack's liquid water over its water. The overhang is a cantilever thinning from a root as thick as it is long to its lip, so the root carries [code]ρ g L[/code] in bending (450 kg/m³ wind-packed snow, heavier with its water); the crack cuts into the section, taking 60% of it when open to a tenth of the length.

method.name: cornice_strength
method.description: The tensile strength of a cornice's root, in kPa: a tenth of the most snow of 450 kg/m³ holds in tension (Sommerfeld 1971), since a slab metres across fails at its weakest flaw (McClung 1979), weakened by melt water in its bonds. A cold, uncracked cornice falls at about 10 m.

method.name: crust_strength
method.description: The pressure, in kPa, a frozen crust of [param thickness] m bears after [param cycles] melt-freeze cycles before it breaks. From the hand hardness of Fierz et al. (2009): a first-cycle crust is one-finger hard (about 19 kPa, so an adult's boot at about 21 kPa breaks it), each further cycle half a step harder (48 kPa after two, pencil hard, 120 kPa, after three). A crust thinner than 2 cm bears in proportion to its thickness.

method.name: get_air_temperature_at
method.description: Returns the air temperature at [param position] in degrees Celsius: the weather temperature cooled by [member lapse_rate] above the weather's ground height.

method.name: get_albedo_at
method.description: Returns the albedo of the snow at [param position]: 0.84 when fresh, ageing toward 0.70 when dry and 0.50 when melting.

method.name: get_blown_flux_max
method.description: The largest snow transport flux on the map in the last update, kg per metre of width per second ([member wind_transport_enabled]).

method.name: get_blown_mean
method.description: The snow water the wind moved in the last update, mm per cell on average.

method.name: get_canopy_capacity_at
method.description: The canopy's capacity over [param position] for fresh snow, in mm.

method.name: get_canopy_load_at
method.description: Snow water held in the tree crowns over [param position], in mm.

method.name: get_catch_texture
method.description: The catch map over the near square (the [code]snow_catch_map[/code] shader global): the height the pack lies at, the canopy's load over its capacity, the canopy closure, and 1 in alpha. Surfaces well under that height (under a roof) stay bare; surfaces well above it under a canopy (tree crowns) show the canopy's load.

method.name: get_cornice_at
method.description: The world tier's cornice at a position: its overhang in metres along the wind that built it, as an XZ vector.

method.name: get_cornice_crack_at
method.description: The opening of the tension crack behind the world tier's cornice at a position, in metres. It opens by creep (see [method cornice_crack_rate]) and fills as the wind builds the cornice on.

method.name: get_cornice_failure_count
method.description: How many cornices have fallen since the world tier was made.

method.name: get_crust_cycles_at
method.description: The melt-freeze cycles of the top crust at [param position] (0: no crust).

method.name: get_crust_depth_at
method.description: The snow over the top crust at [param position], in metres. New snow and snow sliding down bury it, melt uncovers it.

method.name: get_crust_strength_at
method.description: The pressure the top crust at [param position] bears before it breaks, in kPa (see [method crust_strength]); 0 where there is no crust or it is wet. [SnowSurface3D] holds a body whose pressure is lower on the crust, so only the snow over it compacts.

method.name: get_crust_thickness_at
method.description: The thickness of the top crust at [param position], in metres.

method.name: get_density_at
method.description: Returns the density of the snowpack at [param position], in kg/m³.

method.name: get_depth_at
method.description: Returns the depth of snow at [param position], in metres. Outside the near square it reads the world tier when [member climate] has been baked (as do [method get_swe_at], [method get_density_at], [method get_albedo_at] and [method get_wetness_at]).

method.name: get_drift_factor
method.description: Returns how far the wind of the last update was above the blowing-snow threshold, from 0 (calm) to 1. [SnowSurface3D] fills trails with it.

method.name: get_ground_height_at
method.description: Returns the ground height the snowpack uses at [param position].

method.name: get_map_rect
method.description: Returns the world XZ rectangle the map covers.

method.name: get_new_snow_at
method.description: Returns the depth of new snow, in metres, the last update (or [method add_snow]) laid at [param position].

method.name: get_runoff_at
method.description: Returns the water leaving the snowpack at [param position] during the last update, in mm/h: meltwater and rain beyond what the pack holds, or the rain itself on bare ground.

method.name: get_snow_texture
method.description: Returns the snow map texture: depth in metres (R), albedo (G), wetness (B) and density in tonnes per cubic metre (A).

method.name: get_snowfall_rate_at
method.description: Returns the precipitation falling as snow at [param position], in millimetres of water an hour (the snow share of Jennings et al. 2018 at that height). [SnowFall3D] reads it.

method.name: get_swe_at
method.description: Returns the snow water equivalent at [param position], in mm (kg/m²), liquid included.

method.name: get_total_water
method.description: Returns the water held in snow on the whole map, in kg.

method.name: get_update_count
method.description: Returns how many updates the snowpack has run, so other nodes can tell when it changed.

method.name: get_update_time_msec
method.description: Returns how long the last update took on the calling thread, in milliseconds.

method.name: get_wetness_at
method.description: Returns the liquid water in the snowpack at [param position] over what it can hold, 0 (dry) to 1 (saturated).

method.name: get_world_depth_at
method.description: The world tier's snow depth at a position, in metres, even inside the near square.

method.name: get_world_rect
method.description: The world tier's square in world XZ; empty without a baked climate.

method.name: get_world_swe_at
method.description: The world tier's snow water equivalent at a position, in mm.

method.name: get_world_texture
method.description: The world tier's snow map (same channels as the near one), published as the [code]snow_world_map[/code] shader global.

method.name: has_world
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while a baked [member climate] gives the cover a world tier.

method.name: holding_depth
method.description: Returns the snow water equivalent (mm) a slope of [param slope_degrees] holds before it slides (SnowSlide, Bernhardt and Schulz 2010): [param min_mm] at 75 degrees and steeper, growing by a factor of e every 1 / [param decay] degrees flatter.

method.name: new_snow_density
method.description: Returns the density of new snow falling at [param celsius] (Hedstrom and Pomeroy 1998): 67.92 + 51.25 exp(T / 2.59) kg/m³.

method.name: refresh_heights
method.description: Samples the ground again for every cell, after the terrain under the map changed.

method.name: sample_ground_height
method.description: Returns the ground height at [param position] straight from [member height_source] (or a ray down on [member ground_collision_mask]), finer than the cells. NaN where nothing answers.

method.name: snowfall_fraction
method.description: Returns the share of precipitation that falls as snow at air temperature [param celsius] and relative humidity [param humidity] (0 to 1), from the logistic model of Jennings et al. (2018): 1 / (1 + exp(-10.04 + 1.41 T + 0.09 RH)), RH in percent. Half falls as snow at 3.9 °C in dry air (50%) and at 1.4 °C in humid air (90%).

method.name: transport_flux
method.description: The snow the wind carries over lying snow, kg per metre of width per second, at a 10 m wind of [param wind10] m/s over snow of [param density] kg/m³ at [param celsius]: saltation (Pomeroy and Gray 1990) plus suspension, the PBSM concentration profile (Pomeroy and Male 1992) times the log wind profile up to 5 m. 0 at or below [method transport_threshold] and in snow at or above 0 °C.

method.name: transport_threshold
method.description: The 10 m wind, m/s, that starts snow of [param density] kg/m³ at [param celsius] moving: the higher of Li and Pomeroy (1997) by temperature and Liston et al. (2007) by density, u*t = 0.10 exp(0.003 ρ).

members.member: Trees in the [WeatherMap3D]'s canopy hold falling snow in their crowns and unload it later in wind and warmth (Hedstrom and Pomeroy 1998; Roesch et al. 2001).

A baked [SnowClimate]: the cover keeps a coarse world tier of snow over its square, carries it on with the weather at a lower rate, seeds cells entering the near square from it (then sheds what their finer slopes cannot hold) and publishes it as [code]snow_world_map[/code] and [code]snow_world_rect[/code], which [BaseMaterial3D] snow and the path tracer read beyond the near square.

If [code]true[/code], the world tier's cornices open a tension crack behind them by creep and fall once the root cannot hold them (see [method cornice_root_stress] and [method cornice_strength]). The fallen slab lands as dense debris at the foot of the face below, in the world tier and the near square, and [signal cornice_failed] is emitted. Cold cornices hold for weeks; thaws and rain bring them down within days, so most fall in spring.

When on, a surface that was wet (meltwater or rain) and freezes again turns into a crust: "at most a few centimetres thick", harder with each melt-freeze cycle (melt-freeze crust, MFcr, in Fierz et al. 2009). The refrozen water makes it thicker, new snow buries it, melt uncovers it, and a crust wet again bears nothing until it freezes. Only the top crust is kept: when the snow over a buried crust gets wet, a new one starts there.
How far upwind the terrain is searched for shelter (Winstral's dmax), in metres.

If [code]true[/code], wind above [member drift_threshold_wind] moves falling snow into sheltered ground and off exposed ground, by the maximum upwind slope Sx (Winstral, Elder and Davis 2002) over a 30 degree window. The map keeps the snow that fell. Sx is baked on worker threads when the wind turns by more than 10 degrees.

How strongly drift redistributes falling snow: at full wind, a fully sheltered cell gets [code]1 + drift_strength[/code] times the snowfall and a fully exposed cell [code]1 - drift_strength[/code] times.
The 10 m wind speed above which snow drifts, about 7 m/s for dry snow (Li and Pomeroy 1997). Drift is full at twice this speed.
The width of the square map, in metres.
The physics layers cast against for ground heights where [member height_source] gives none.
Relative humidity (0 to 1) used when no [code]WeatherMap3D[/code] is in the scene.
How fast the air cools with height above the weather map's ground height, in °C per km (6.5, the standard atmosphere). Sets where rain turns to snow on a mountain and where snow stays.
The share of its ice the snowpack holds as liquid water before meltwater and rain drain out.

Melt per watt of absorbed sunlight (mm m² h⁻¹ W⁻¹), the SRF of Pellicciotti et al. (2005). The sunlight is the clear-sky beam from [member sun_light] (Meinel and Meinel 1976) on each cell's slope, through the cloud shadow or cover of the weather map, times one minus the snow's albedo.
Melt per degree above zero (mm h⁻¹ °C⁻¹), the TF of Pellicciotti et al. (2005). Meltwater also refreezes at this rate below 0 °C.
Snow melts only above this air temperature, in °C.
How much more precipitation falls per 100 m above the reference height, as a share (orographic enhancement); 0 keeps it even.
Precipitation in mm/h of water used when no [code]WeatherMap3D[/code] is in the scene. With one, the map's rain rate is used, split into rain and snow.

If [code]true[/code], the map is published as the [code]snow_map[/code] and [code]snow_map_rect[/code] global shader parameters that [member BaseMaterial3D.snow_enabled] reads, in raster and under path tracing.
The number of cells along each side of the map.

With a [member height_source], colliders on these layers (roofs, overhangs) found above the terrain catch the snow, and the ground under them stays bare. Without a height source the cast on [member ground_collision_mask] finds them already.
Ground steeper than this, in degrees, sheds snow beyond what it holds (SnowSlide: 25 degrees).

If [code]true[/code], snow slides off steep ground to lower cells (SnowSlide, Bernhardt and Schulz 2010): from the highest snow surface down, a cell holding more than [method holding_depth] passes the excess downhill, in proportion to the drop to each lower neighbour. Mass is conserved.
How fast the snow a slope holds grows as it gets flatter, per degree below 75. See [method holding_depth].
Weather seconds between slide passes.
The snow water equivalent (mm) slopes of 75 degrees and steeper still hold.
Updates per real second.
The distance, in metres, over which [member wind_transport_enabled] measures the ground's curvature (MicroMet's length scale; at least two cells).

When on, wind above the transport threshold moves the snow already lying (SnowTran-3D, Liston and Sturm 1998): each cell sends its flux ([method transport_flux]) downwind, so snow leaves where the wind speeds up (windward shoulders, crests) and settles where it slows (below crests, in hollows), laid down wind-packed at 300 kg/m³. The wind over the ground is weighted by its slope along the wind and its curvature (MicroMet, Liston and Elder 2006). Snow under a frozen crust, wet snow and snow under trees stay. Snow comes in at the upwind edge of the map as from a cell like the edge one and leaves at the downwind edge. [member drift_enabled] is separate: it places falling snow.
How many updates of the near square pass between updates of the world tier.

signal.name: cornice_failed
signal.description: Emitted when a cornice falls: [param position] the crest top it broke from, [param direction] out over the lee, [param length] its overhang in metres and [param mass] the snow that fell, in kg. [SnowCornice3D] turns it into falling blocks near the camera.
